playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a central cell (5) on the first round unless I have a specific reason not to; on later rounds change my hide if opponents show a repeatable pattern that lets them exploit me.

When another boat has just hit me and that boat will fire on me again under the standing order, move my hide away from the previously hit cell next round.

When the standing order tells me who to fire at, fire at that station unless firing at Harbor is ordered — do not fire on Harbor (the penalty is worse than any gain).

When choosing a shot coordinate with no information, pick the middle cell (5); if I have information (previous hits/misses by me or observed patterns from others) bias the shot toward the most-likely cell from that evidence.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, file the same public claim as the office expects (claim truthfully); do not fabricate hits — either the rules or opponents will punish/uncover lies.

When deciding on an escort claim, only claim an escort if there is mutual benefit and plausible evidence (i.e., I can expect another boat to name me too); otherwise claim none. Prioritize making a matching escort claim with one trusted boat if that boat can be persuaded — mutual escorts are +5 each.

When posting notes, keep them short and consistent with team discipline unless I want to bait someone; use neutral observatory phrasing to avoid painting a target on myself.

When I notice an opponent using a simple alternating or small-cycle hiding pattern, vary my own hides and shots unpredictably to avoid becoming their target.

If I get reliable private information about another boat’s location (e.g., I scored a hit), use it offensively in my next shot selection if I will fire at them again; if I won’t, keep that information for coordinating escort claims only.

When in doubt between two reasonable moves, choose the conservative one that avoids provoking Harbor or giving away easy score to an opponent.

1.text:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: alternate between central (4–6) and off-center (2–3 or 7–8) choices each round; do not repeat the exact same cell two rounds in a row.

When notes are requested, be short and noncommittal: give a neutral station-status line (e.g., "steady on station", "holding sector") rather than revealing position or intent.

When the standing order tells me a target, follow it and fire at that named boat unless there is a clear, danger-avoiding reason not to (see Harbor rule).

When choosing a firing cell, shift my hidden cell relative to my previous hides (±2–3 cells) so my shots are not trivially predictable; avoid always firing the same number I hide in if that makes me predictable to others.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, report exactly that result publicly. Do not lie about hit/miss.

When I get a hit on a rival boat, accept it: claim hit and continue pressing that boat in subsequent rounds if standing order requires.

Never fire on Harbor. The penalty for attacking Harbor is larger than the benefit; avoid provoking Harbor’s jettison threat.

When salvaging/claiming an escort, claim another boat only when I have high confidence they will reciprocate (explicit pre-play agreement, or a very clear in-play sign they will name me). Otherwise claim none.

When I am forced into a risky choice between a possible escort point and the risk of being wrong, choose none.

When notes from others are visible as repeated neutral signals, mirror that neutrality to avoid painting myself as a target.

When the score is close near the endgame, tighten hiding randomness (use small variations) to protect accumulated points rather than trying speculative hits.

If I observe a clear pattern in another boat’s hides from revealed hit/miss reports, exploit that pattern in my shot choices, but still maintain plausible deniability in notes.

If an opponent has been hit multiple times and is low on points, deprioritize escort claims aimed at them (they are unlikely to reciprocate) and instead keep shooting per standing order.

When in doubt about whether an action will reveal my hidden cell or commit me to an unreciprocated escort, choose the safer option that preserves points (neutral note, salvage none, honest claim).

2.text:
When I choose a hide cell, pick a centrally located cell (4–6) early to minimize being flanked; in last round pick a cell that risks the least based on current leaders (if I need to steal points, bias toward cells that I have used before to exploit opponents’ likely guesses).

When posting my station note, match the formation tone if I want to avoid drawing attention; post an innocuous, steady message unless I am deliberately trying to bait or signal an alliance.

When the standing order gives a target, follow it by default to avoid being singled out, unless there is a clear tactical reason to deviate (see next rules).

When deciding whether to break the standing order, do so only if: I can kill a leading opponent for a net gain that moves me into first, or I can safely attack Harbor to take the payroll (only if the payoff exceeds the retaliation risk). Otherwise obey.

When selecting a fire cell against a target, favor central cells (4–6) on early/mid rounds to maximize overlap with opponents’ likely hides; in late/decisive rounds bias toward cells I have actually used previously if I suspect opponents are matching my pattern.

When I learn privately my shot was a hit, always claim hit publicly (the rule requires it to match private result).

When I learn privately my shot was a miss, do not automatically lie. Only claim a miss when: I want to avoid immediate retaliation and the expected future loss from lying (being exposed) exceeds the short-term benefit. Recognize that claiming false hits/misses can mislead but risks escalation and loss of trust; use lying sparingly and with a plan to exploit the misinformation.

When considering firing on Harbor, remember the fixed payroll transfer: only attack Harbor if the 3-point transfer plus strategic position (removing Harbor’s deterrent) is worth the likely response; otherwise avoid.

When making an escort claim, name another boat only if I expect mutual naming or a credible reciprocal claim (so I can collect 5 points). Do not claim to escort an unknown or non-participating boat; avoid one-sided escort claims because they yield nothing and may reveal my intentions.

When my opponent pattern shows repeated misses/hits, exploit predictable targeting by shifting my hide to a cell that would have caused their last miss to become a hit, but only if I can anticipate their targeting strategy.

When I am behind on points late in the game, take higher-risk moves: deviate from formation, lie more aggressively, and attempt Harbor attacks or unexpected targets to swing scoring.

When I am ahead late in the game, avoid risky deviations and reduce lying; play conservatively to preserve the lead.

When I receive no information about others’ escorts or intentions, default to salvage: none, unless a clear mutual benefit exists.

When a claimed hit by another is inconsistent with observed outcomes or timing, mark them as untrustworthy and plan to avoid reciprocating their favors; do not immediately punish unless I can do so profitably.

Do not hide on extreme edge cells (1 or 9) as a default because they reduce overlap with others and make hits less likely unless I have a specific read that opponents favor centrals.

If I try deception and it is exposed (opponents respond in ways that reduce my score), stop deception and revert to truthful claims and conservative play for the remainder of the patrol.
